description:
FILED s494 (Fable, 2026-09-21) so the two remaining questions of docs/questions-worth-asking.md have an owner.  Nothing is built.
Q8 -- "How would a user ever find out PCL gave a wrong answer?"  Today: they would not.  68 of 103 everyday programs are byte-identical to perl (s492), 478 of 655 Rosetta programs (s493), and 77 of the Rosetta differences are SILENT.  The project's whole method is "perl is the oracle"; `--check` hands that method to the user for the one program they care about.  SHAPE: `pcl --check x.pl ARGS` = run `perl x.pl ARGS` and `pcl x.pl ARGS` with the same stdin (a file or /dev/null; refuse a TTY stdin unless --stdin FILE), in separate temp cwd copies ONLY if --isolate is given (a program with side effects runs TWICE -- say so loudly in --help: this is for programs that are safe to run twice), compare stdout byte for byte and the exit status, print `identical` or the first differing line with both versions and a one-line invitation to report it (the issue template wants exactly this: the program, perl's line, PCL's line).  The scratch prototype exists: ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s493/bin/diffrun.pl.  COST: a day including docs and a tools/t test; no runtime or compiler change.  RISKS to rule on: perl must be on PATH (it is -- PCL needs perl to transpile); nondeterministic programs (time, rand, hash order) report false differences -- document `PERL_HASH_SEED=0` and that --check is for deterministic output.
Q6 -- "Which of our numbers flatter us?"  The sweep says 96.5 % of rows; the core modules' own t/ says 68 %; the everyday battery 66 %; Rosetta 73 %.  README quotes the first kind.  PROPOSAL: (1) README / STATUS carry the everyday and module-surface numbers beside the suite number once #2099 (everyday-smoke) and #2106 (core-module leg) exist as instruments -- the USER words it; (2) `tools/t/readme-claims.t`: each quantitative claim in README / docs/STATUS.md is tagged in the source (an HTML comment naming the instrument + the blessed number), and the test compares the tag with the instrument's baseline file, failing when the README is STALE in either direction (s493 found two stale claims by hand: the `@_`-aliasing bullet and the pack rows).  Not in the gate (it reads baselines, not the compiler); run at tag time and by #494's doc-refresh step.
DECISIONS WANTED FROM THE USER: build `--check`? (Fable recommends yes, after the two in-flight everyday batches merge -- it is the cheapest way to make the alpha honest); the README wording for the second kind of number.


=== USER RULING s494 (2026-09-21) ===
"For 3, if you think it would be a helpful tool then do it."  Fable: yes -- APPROVED, `pcl --check` is to be BUILT.  DESIGN + BRIEF: ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s494/s494k/prompt.md (label s494k, IDs 2275-2284): the oracle is $^X (the perl running pcl), stdin /dev/null unless --check-stdin, STDOUT compared byte for byte, exit status compared by CLASS, STDERR never compared but its line count reported (the USER's error bar is "fail in the same places", not the text); verdicts IDENTICAL / SAME FAILURE / DIFFERENT OUTPUT / ONLY PERL FAILED / ONLY PCL FAILED / cannot check; exit 0 / 1 / 2; PCL_CHECK_SIDE exported to each child (documented; makes the test deterministic); --help says the program RUNS TWICE.  NOT launched in s494 (USER: no new subjobs this session) -- FIRST launch next session.  The Q6 half (`readme-claims` test) waits for the instruments #2099 and #2106.

=== DONE (s494k, 2026-09-25): the `pcl --check` HALF (Q8) === Status left OPEN on purpose: the Q6 half (`tools/t/readme-claims.t`) is NOT built — it still waits for #2106.
Built as designed: `pcl --check [opts] script.pl|-e CODE [args]`; oracle $^X; the PCL side re-invokes the same `pcl` without --check; STDOUT byte for byte, exit status by CLASS, stderr line counts only; verdicts IDENTICAL / SAME FAILURE [0], DIFFERENT OUTPUT / ONLY PERL|PCL FAILED / DIFFERENT FAILURE [1], cannot check [2]; --check-stdin FILE, --check-keep DIR; PCL_CHECK_SIDE=perl|pcl in each child; the issues URL read from README.md (tools/install-pcl now installs README.md).  Code tools/lib/PCLCheck.pm (loaded only under --check), docs/pcl-check.md, pointers in docs/STATUS.md (Known sharp edges) and CONTRIBUTING.md (Reporting a bug), CHANGELOG.
Numbers: tools/t/pcl-check.t 41/41; tools/t/install-pcl.t 60/60; gate 261/8654 PASS (= main); everyday corpus (122 programs) --check agree/differ = diffrun.pl's on 122 of 122; plain `pcl trivial.pl` byte-identical, 20-run medians before 0.0389/0.0383 s, after 0.0386/0.0368 s.
Found by --check itself: #2275 (the pcl driver keeps a literal `--` in @ARGV).
subject: APPROVED s494 (USER: "if you think it would be a helpful tool then do it"; from the meta list Q8 + Q6): `pcl --check script.pl [args]` -- run the program under perl AND under PCL, compare stdout + exit status (+ optionally stderr's line count), print the first difference -- so every user becomes a differential tester and a wrong answer stops being SILENT; and, from Q6, a checked-in `tools/t/readme-claims.t` that turns every number in README / STATUS into an assertion that fails when it stops being true in EITHER direction
